blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Mesoscale eddies carry most of the ocean's kinetic energy and move heat, salt and nutrients across basins, yet where an eddy will be two weeks ahead is still read off ocean models with post-hoc tracking heuristics. We introduce HaiRuo, which forecasts eddies as fields and as objects at once: from 30 days of satellite sea-level maps, one forward pass returns 15 days of sea level and geostrophic velocity, daily eddy masks and the trajectory of every eddy alive today. HaiRuo pairs two components with a clear division of labour: (1) HaiRuo-1B, an open-weight 1.05-billion-parameter foundation model pretrained without labels on 24 years of global satellite-altimetry observations, which supplies the 15-day physical fields and masks (+0.14 field skill and +1.1 mIoU points under the same decoder) and further lowers 15-day centre error by 1.2 km frozen (1.35 km over training from scratch); and (2) XuanJi, a Lagrangian object decoder that samples the evolving forecast in each eddy's co-moving polar frame and refines the 15-day path across three look-ahead rounds, removing 2.5 km on HaiRuo-1B (2.9 km with joint fine-tuning) and 2.5-3.3 km via its object attention across six published backbones. Under one pre-registered global evaluation over the whole ocean, HaiRuo improves on fourteen methods on every endpoint (25.2 vs. 30.6 km 15-day centre error, -18%), holding its margin outside the labelled regions and through both phases of the El Nino-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), while reproducing westward drift, 50-60 deg S eastward reversal and poleward cyclone-anticyclone deflection. Over ten days through one fixed tracker, HaiRuo's forecast field cuts the eddy-centre error of WenHai and XiHe by 37-43% (-2.8 km vs. day 0 while they degrade +4.3-8.7 km), and its object trajectories cut pipeline error by 77-78% globally. Open-weight checkpoints, code and project page: https://github.com/xkqin/HaiRuo
blocks.zh: 中尺度的编织物携带着海洋的大部分动能,并跨盆地移动出热量,盐和养分,然而,一个eddy会提前两周的地方仍然读取有后热跟踪热量的海洋模型. 我们介绍海路(HaiRuo),它同时预测被作为田地和物体:从卫星海平面图的30天起,一个前行传回了15天的海平面和地心营养速度,每天的埃迪口罩以及今天活生生的每一个埃迪的行道. HaiRuo对两个有明确分工的构件:(1) HaiRuo-1B,一个开放式的105亿参数地基模型,在24年的全球卫星-时空观测上未经标记就预先训练,它提供15天物理场和口罩(+0.14场技能,并在同一解码器下加1.1米U点),并将15天中心误差进一步降低1.2公里被冻结(1.35公里从零开始训练);和(2)XuanJi,一个拉格朗格天体解码器,它通过它6个已公布的主干体的物体注意去除HaiRuo-1B上2.5公里(2.9公里同微调)和2.5-3.3公里。 根据预先登记的关于整个海洋的全球评价,海鲁奥改进了每个终点的14个方法(25.2对30.6公里15天中心误差为-18%),在标定区域之外和在El Nino-Southern Osciation(ENOSO)的两个阶段保持了边距,同时再现了向西漂移、50-60德克S向东转向和向上气旋-反环状偏转。 HaiRuo的预测场通过一个固定的跟踪器将温海和西贺的eddy-centre误差减少了37-43%(2.8公里对0天,同时降解+4.3-8.7公里),其物体轨迹将管道误差全球减少了77-78%. 开放式检查站、代码和项目网页:https://github.com/xkqin/HaiRuo

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Where will this eddy be in two weeks? Mesoscale eddies, coherent vortices 50–300 km across that live for weeks to months, carry most of the
ocean’s kinetic energy and move heat, salt and nutrients across basins [ 6 , 15 ] . Satellites have mapped them every day for three decades, and atlases detect and track the
eddies the maps resolve [ 35 , 14 ] . Forecasting them is a different matter. Run a state-of-the-art AI ocean
forecaster [ 8 , 46 ] and track the eddies in its forecast with a fixed tracker, and they land farther from their true
positions than if the forecaster’s own initial state had been held fixed (Section 4.5 ).
blocks.zh:
两周后Eddy会在哪里? 中尺度的编织器,50-300公里长的 连续的涡流, 活了几周到几个月,
海洋的动能和移动热量、盐和营养物质跨越盆地[6、15]。 30年来,卫星每天绘制地图,地图集探测并跟踪
编辑地图解决[35,14]. 预测是另一回事 运行最先进的AI海洋
预测器[8,46] 并用固定的跟踪器追踪其预测中的编辑,它们着陆距离真实的更远
比起预测员自己的初始状态是否固定(第4.5节)。

blocks.en:
The reason is structural. These systems forecast fields, learn from reanalysis, and leave eddies to a tracker applied afterwards; nothing in
them follows an eddy. Seen from computer vision, eddy forecasting is coupled field-and-object forecasting on continuous spherical fields, where eddies are coherent vortices defined by gradients of the evolving flow itself: given 30
daily maps, predict the next 15, the daily cyclonic and anticyclonic masks, and the path of every eddy alive today. We find that the object belongs in the decoder : a forecaster should learn the ocean’s dynamics at scale from what satellites observe, and then
read eddies out as objects that follow and re-sample its own evolving forecast.
blocks.zh:
原因是结构性的。 这些系统预测字段,从再分析中学习,然后将 Eddies 留给一个之后应用的跟踪器;无
他们跟随一个Eddy。 从计算机视野来看,eddy预报是对连续球面的场-对象相接的预测,其中eddies是由演化流本身的梯度所定义的连贯的漩涡:给定了30
每日地图,预测接下来的15个,每日的"环球"和"反环球口罩",以及今天活生生的每一个Eddy的道路. 我们发现该物体属于解码器:预报员应该从卫星观测到的尺度上学习海洋的动力学,然后
将 Eddies 读出为遵循并重新取出自身演化预测的对象。

blocks.en:
We present HaiRuo (Figure 1 ). Existing AI ocean models [ 8 , 46 , 50 , 13 , 23 ] are reanalysis state emulators rather than open, label-free observation foundation backbones for downstream decoders. Our backbone, HaiRuo-1B, fills this gap: a 1.05-billion-parameter foundation model pretrained without labels on 24 years of
global satellite-altimetry observations with a two-stage spherical 0.5 ∘ 0.5^{\circ} stem, dual-rate 30-day memory, eddy-focused chirality-gated attention, multi-axis masked reconstruction and a geostrophic flow-advected contrast. Every readout tested benefits from HaiRuo-1B, and we pair it with XuanJi, a Lagrangian object decoder that returns 15-day fields, daily masks and every eddy’s trajectory via XuanJi object attention : unlike static-map motion queries [ 38 , 52 ] , occupancy grids [ 21 , 22 ] or point-vortex advection, XuanJi re-samples the model’s own continuous evolving 15-day forecast and backbone along each eddy’s predicted path in a co-moving polar frame (mean intensity, self-advection dipole and strain quadrupole modes), attends across all 15 leads, and averages four refiners over three look-ahead rounds.

blocks.en:
Our contributions are:
(i) HaiRuo-1B , an open-weight 1.05B ocean foundation model pretrained without labels on 24 years of global altimetry observations ,
forecasting 15-day sea level and geostrophic velocity in one pass and lifting every readout tested: under XuanJi, it raises field skill from 0.63 to 0.77, adds 1.1 mIoU points and lowers D15 by 1.2 km frozen on Dev48 (1.35 km over training the same 1B architecture from scratch, and 0.6–1.4 km over six video backbones), while even with plain base heads frozen HaiRuo-1B (25.8 km) beats all 14 baselines and self-supervised PredRNN-V2 (30.4 km frozen, 26.6 km fine-tuned);
(ii) XuanJi , a plug-and-play co-moving polar object decoder that samples azimuthal Fourier modes of the evolving forecast along each eddy’s predicted orbit and refines all 15 leads jointly across three look-ahead rounds and four refiners, removing 2.5 km of D15 on HaiRuo-1B on Dev48 ( 2.9 km with joint fine-tuning; 0.56 km on Dev48 and 0.87 km globally from multi-expert refinement) and 2.5–3.3 km via two-round object attention across six published backbones;
(iii) a pre-registered global evaluation (Table 1 , Figure 3 ) in which HaiRuo improves on fourteen methods on every endpoint , lowering D15 by 18 % against the strongest and by 17–18 % outside the labelled regions and in both ENSO phases, while reproducing latitudinal westward drift (and 50–60 ∘ S eastward reversal) and poleward cyclone–anticyclone deflection; and
(iv) a system comparison through one fixed tracker over days 1–10, in which HaiRuo’s forecast field cuts the
eddy-centre error of WenHai and XiHe by 37–43 % field for field on Test48 (improving by 2.8 km over its held-fixed day-0 state while they degrade by 4.3–8.7 km), and direct object trajectories cut pipeline error by 77–78 % over the whole ocean.

blocks.en:
Eddy atlases detect eddies as closed sea-surface-height contours (earlier, by Okubo–Weiss [ 5 ] ) and link them in time [ 6 , 35 , 30 ] ; EddyNet [ 27 ] learns detection. Trajectory forecasters model each track from its own attributes via recurrent [ 47 ] , transformer [ 10 ] , dual-graph [ 11 ] and LSTM/Informer [ 19 ] networks, or via physics-fused [ 51 ] and global [ 7 ] models without public code, seeing
at most local field descriptors. HaiRuo forecasts fields, masks and tracks jointly, reading its own forecast around every moving eddy.

blocks.en:
Learned ocean forecasters (XiHe [ 46 ] , WenHai [ 8 ] ,
LangYa [ 50 ] , GLONET [ 13 ] , FuXi-Ocean [ 23 ] ) train on reanalysis from assimilated three-dimensional
states and forecast state variables rather than eddy objects [ 12 ] . Altimetry interpolators [ 2 ] and climate emulators [ 9 ] likewise do not forecast eddies as objects, and open foundation backbones pretrained on global ocean observations remain scarce.
Earth-system foundation models (Aurora [ 4 ] , Prithvi WxC [ 37 ] ,
ClimaX [ 32 ] ) pretrain on atmospheric reanalyses and climate simulations with one- to two-step histories
and ≥ 1 ∘ \geq 1^{\circ} tokens. HaiRuo-1B pretrains directly on altimetry observations with a 30-day context and 0.5 ∘ 0.5^{\circ} eddy-resolving tokens, matched to eddies that drift a few kilometres per day with a 50 km median
radius.

Deformable attention [ 53 ] and slot attention [ 29 ] gather
evidence where the object is, and object-centric video predictors roll slots forward in time [ 49 ] . In motion
forecasting and planning, MTR [ 38 ] and QCNet [ 52 ] refine trajectories with static map features gathered around their own

polar rings where the eddy is going , decomposes each ring into azimuthal Fourier modes ( m = 0 , 1 , 2 m{=}0,1,2 ), and re-estimates all 15 leads jointly.

3.2 HaiRuo-1B: pretrained foundation backbone

blocks.en:
A two-stage spherical stem embeds each daily map into fine tokens at 0.5 ∘ 0.5^{\circ} (patch 4), so a 50 km-radius eddy spans one to two tokens without aliasing; two spherical stride-2
convolutions build a three-level pyramid at 0.5 ∘ 0.5^{\circ} , 1 ∘ 1^{\circ} and 2 ∘ 2^{\circ} (depths 6/10/20), with a learned quality gate damping poorly observed swaths. To capture month-scale evolution without quadratic cost, the 30-day history is compressed at two rates: the last
seven days stay explicit and the preceding 23 are distilled by per-token softmax routing into eight chronological memory slots (15 steps in total), keeping all 30 days on a differentiable path. The
three levels stack 36 eddy-focused spatio-temporal blocks: spatial attention combines validity-masked shifted windows with soft eddy-vorticity focus, core–ring deformable sampling and chirality-gated projections, while temporal attention applies physical day-age-aligned QKV routing across the 15 steps. A bank of 240 sparse eddy route-memory tokens and global latents [ 24 ] bridges the pyramid to a multi-scale field
decoder that queries each lead, fuses the three levels through longitude-periodic residual blocks, and outputs all 15 daily residuals for the six fields in one pass, F ^ l = F 0 + δ l ⊙ r l , \hat{F}_{l}=F_{0}+\delta_{l}\odot r_{l}, (1) where F 0 F_{0} is the last observed field and δ l \delta_{l} the training RMS of the l l -day change; zero-initialised r l r_{l} starts every

La Niña winters from the Oceanic Niño Index (ONI) [ 33 ] .

reproduce altimetry propagation statistics [ 6 ] (Appendix ): across global latitude bins
the 15-day westward drift matches observations ( r = 0.98 r{=}0.98 , slope 1.14, reversing to eastward at 50–60 ∘ S), and unlike constant-velocity extrapolation (which inherits zonal drift but reverses meridional polarity deflection in both hemispheres) cyclones drift poleward relative to anticyclones in both hemispheres, closer to observations than PredRNN-V2. blocks.en: Table 3 and Table separate the roles of the foundation backbone and the object decoder on Dev48: HaiRuo-1B supplies the physical fields and masks and lifts every readout tested, while XuanJi refines the trajectories of every backbone it reads (HaiRuo: 22.87 km).

blocks.en:
Under the same XuanJi decoder, frozen HaiRuo-1B lifts field skill from 0.63 to 0.77 ( + 0.141 +0.141 ), adds 1.09 mIoU points and
removes 1.19 km of D15 over no backbone (25.07 to 23.85 km): all of the gain of HaiRuo over the decoder alone in fields, most in masks and over half in
trajectories comes from the pretrained representation. Trained from scratch, the identical 1B + + XuanJi model scores 24.22 km, 66.52 % mIoU and 0.662 field skill, losing 1.35 km D15, 1.12 mIoU and 0.107 field skill to HaiRuo (trailing even frozen HaiRuo-1B by 0.93 km). Under the same two-round XuanJi decoder, frozen HaiRuo-1B also leads all six published video-prediction backbones on every endpoint: by 0.57–1.44 km D15, 0.80–1.85 mIoU and 0.074–0.142 field skill, every interval excluding zero (Table ). Even with plain base heads (no object attention), frozen HaiRuo-1B (25.76 km, 67.10 % mIoU, 0.771 field skill) beats all 14 baselines and 22-epoch self-supervised PredRNN-V2 pretrained on the same global altimetry record (30.36 km / 63.31 % / 0.735 frozen; 26.58 km / 66.84 % / 0.739 fine-tuned; Table , Appendix ). Across backbone scales, field skill and mIoU grow from 200M ( + 0.014 +0.014 – 0.059 0.059 field skill, + 0.06 +0.06 – 0.34 0.34 mIoU) to 1B (where D15 also drops by 0.45 0.45 km at 1 ∘ 1^{\circ} and 1.19 1.19 km at 0.5 ∘ 0.5^{\circ} ), with the two-stage 0.5 ∘ 0.5^{\circ} stem and eddy-focused spatio-temporal blocks ablated in Table (Appendix ).

Attached as a plug-in to six published backbones, two-round XuanJi object attention lowers D15 on every one of them by 2.49–3.34 km while leaving masks and fields unchanged (Figure , Table ). On frozen HaiRuo-1B, two-round object attention removes 1.91 km of D15 (25.76 to 23.85 km; − 2.08 -2.08 km on the 1 ∘ 1^{\circ} 1B backbone), with both multi-round sampling ( + 0.28 +0.28 km at one round) and cross-lead attention ( + 0.12 +0.12 km when removed) contributing (Table 3 ). Full three-round four-expert look-ahead refinement with EMA removes another 0.56 km on Dev48 (23.29 km; − 0.77 -0.77 km on Test48, − 0.87 -0.87 km globally), and joint fine-tuning (HaiRuo, 22.87 km; − 2.89 -2.89 km total) removes another 0.42 km on Dev48 ( − 0.34 -0.34 km on Test48, − 0.21 -0.21 km globally) while adding 0.36–0.78 mIoU points.

blocks.en: 4.5 Comparison with global ocean forecasters
blocks.zh: 4.5 与全球海洋预测器的比较

blocks.en:
We evaluate the released global AI ocean forecasters WenHai [ 8 ] and XiHe [ 46 ] (from GLORYS12 [ 26 ] , WenHai forced by ERA5) on the 48 test dates at two levels (Appendix ): (i) field-for-field through the same fixed tracker on Test48, HaiRuo’s forecast field
scores 29.5 km, cutting WenHai (47.1 km) and XiHe (51.6 km) by 37–43 %, landing within 0.52 km of true altimetry (29.0 km), and improving by 2.8 km over its held-fixed day-0 state (32.3 km) while WenHai and XiHe degrade by 4.3 and 8.7 km beyond theirs (42.9 km); (ii) as objects , HaiRuo’s trajectories score 10.1 km on Test48 (79–80 % lower) and 11.2 km globally (Figure b, Table ), 77–78 % below WenHai (48.0 km) and XiHe (52.0 km), bypassing the 18.8 km tracker offset on true altimetry and 10.6 km day-0 reanalysis offset.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
HaiRuo forecasts mesoscale eddies as fields and objects from satellite altimetry. Pretrained without labels on 24 years of global altimetry, the open-weight 1.05B foundation model
HaiRuo-1B supplies the physical fields and masks and lifts every readout tested, while XuanJi refines eddy trajectories on every backbone it reads; together they beat all 14 methods on every endpoint of a
pre-registered global protocol, cutting D15 by 18 % overall and 17–18 % outside the labelled regions and in both ENSO phases, while reproducing westward drift (and 50–60 ∘ S eastward reversal) and poleward cyclone–anticyclone deflection. Open-weight checkpoints, code, pre-registration record and the project page will be available at https://github.com/xkqin/HaiRuo .
